steps.message:
The change is one line (`routes/users.js:6`), but it's a breaking change to a published contract, so I want your go-ahead before making it.

`userId` is the field the `GET /users` response hands to clients. `README.md:3-5` names three consumers — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and states that field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. Renaming in place means any consumer reading `userId` gets `undefined` at the next deploy; the iOS clients in particular can't be updated in lockstep.

questions.question: How should the userId → user_id rename be delivered given the documented /users contract?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside the existing userId in the /users response. Non-breaking: existing consumers keep working while clients migrate, and userId can be dropped later once the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export are all off it.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README's stated process: leave /users as-is and add a versioned variant (e.g. /v2/users) that returns user_id. Cleanest response shape, but more code than a one-line edit and needs routing decisions.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Replace userId with user_id in the existing /users response, exactly as asked. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated. Choose this if those consumers are already handled or the contract note is stale.
